name: Random Forest
description: Random Forest is an ensemble learning method that constructs multiple decision trees and aggregates their predictions. It uses bootstrap aggregating (bagging) and random feature selection to create diverse trees, reducing overfitting and improving prediction accuracy over single decision trees.

concept.ensembleMethod: Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregating) - trains trees on random subsets of data
concept.randomFeatureSelection: At each split, only a random subset of features is considered
concept.outOfBagError: Estimate of prediction error using samples not selected in bootstrap
concept.explanation: Each tree is trained on a bootstrap sample (random sampling with replacement). Feature randomness at splits ensures tree diversity. The ensemble averages out individual tree errors.

idealScenarios: When decision tree overfitting is a concern
When interpretability is less critical than accuracy
avoidWhen: When model size is limited (many trees = large model)
When exact prediction reasoning is required

nEstimators.impact: More trees = better performance but slower; diminishing returns after 100-500

maxDepth.impact: Limits overfitting; null = unlimited (trees grow until pure)

minSamplesSplit.description: Minimum samples to split internal node

maxFeatures.description: Features to consider at each split
maxFeatures.impact: Lower = more tree diversity, less correlation

oobScore.impact: Provides unbiased error estimate without separate validation set

preprocessing: Handle missing values (Random Forest can handle them)
training: Create n bootstrap samples from training data
For each sample, train a decision tree
At each node, randomly select max_features features
Grow tree until stopping criteria (no pruning)
prediction: Aggregate predictions (vote for classification, average for regression)
evaluation: Compare to single decision tree baseline

complexity.interpretability: Medium - feature importance available but no single tree

pros: Reduces overfitting vs single decision trees
cons: Can overfit with noisy data if depth unlimited
Biased toward features with more categories
Not ideal for very high-dimensional sparse data

featureImportance.calculation: Total decrease in node impurity weighted by probability of reaching node
featureImportance.limitations: Biased toward high-cardinality features; use permutation importance for better accuracy

variants.extraTrees: Extremely Randomized Trees - more randomness in split thresholds
